hints: A thorough comparison must address both where the data is centred and how spread out it is.
Name one measure of average (such as median or mean) and one measure of variation (such as IQR or standard deviation).

walkthrough.text:
State the first essential component (measure of location):
$$\text{Central tendency: describes typical/average value (e.g. median or mean)}$$

State the second essential component (measure of dispersion):
$$\text{Spread/dispersion: describes variation or consistency (e.g. IQR or standard deviation)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify centre:
$$\text{Measure of central tendency (mean/median)}$$

Identify spread:
$$\text{Measure of dispersion (IQR/standard deviation)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify central tendency (measure of average or location) with an example such as mean, median, or mode.
Identify spread (measure of variation, dispersion, or consistency) with an example such as standard deviation, IQR, or range.

hints: Remember that grouped data calculations use class midpoints and class frequencies, not the individual raw numbers.

hints: For $n = 8$, split into two halves of 4 items: lower is $74, 78, 81, 83$ and upper is $86, 90, 92, 97$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the median of the 8 runners:

Find the quartiles of the two 4-item halves:
$$Q_1 = \frac{78 + 81}{2} = 79.5\text{ min},\quad Q_3 = \frac{90 + 92}{2} = 91.0\text{ min}$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 91.0 - 79.5 = 11.5\text{ minutes}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:

$$\text{IQR} = 91 - 79.5 = 11.5\text{ minutes}$$

hints: Variance is invariant under a shift: $\text{Var}(x) = \text{Var}(y) = \frac{\sum y^2}{n} - (\bar{y})^2$.
Compute the standard deviation: $\sigma_x = \sqrt{0.1916} \approx 0.438\text{ mm}$ (to 3 s.f.).

walkthrough.text:
Find the mean of the coded variable and decode to $x$:
$$\bar{y} = \frac{\sum (x - 20)}{10} = \frac{4.2}{10} = 0.42$$
$$\bar{x} = 20 + 0.42 = 20.42\text{ mm}$$

Compute the variance using the coded sums:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \text{Var}(y) = \frac{\sum y^2}{n} - (\bar{y})^2 = \frac{3.68}{10} - (0.42)^2 = 0.368 - 0.1764 = 0.1916\text{ mm}^2$$

Take the square root to determine the standard deviation:
$$\sigma_x = \sqrt{0.1916} \approx 0.4377 = 0.438\text{ mm (3 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find coded mean and add 20:
$$\bar{x} = 20 + 0.42 = 20.42\text{ mm}$$

Square root for standard deviation:
$$\sqrt{0.1916} = 0.438\text{ mm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate mean of coded variable y = x - 20 as 4.2 / 10 = 0.42 and hence mean of x = 20 + 0.42 = 20.42 mm.
Calculate standard deviation of x = sqrt(0.1916) = 0.4377 mm (or 0.438 mm to 3 s.f.).

hints: Compute $\text{IQR} = 20.7 - 20.1 = 0.6\text{ mm}$.
Calculate $1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 0.9\text{ mm}$.
Lower fence is $20.1 - 0.9 = 19.2\text{ mm}$; Upper fence is $20.7 + 0.9 = 21.6\text{ mm}$.
Compare $19.4$ and $21.8$ to these fences.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate IQR and range:
$$\text{IQR} = 20.7 - 20.1 = 0.6\text{ mm},\quad \text{Range} = 21.8 - 19.4 = 2.4\text{ mm}$$

Compute fence boundaries using the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule:
$$1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 1.5 \times 0.6 = 0.9\text{ mm}$$
$$\text{Lower fence} = 20.1 - 0.9 = 19.2\text{ mm},\quad \text{Upper fence} = 20.7 + 0.9 = 21.6\text{ mm}$$

Test both endpoints:
$$\text{Min } 19.4 \ge 19.2 \implies \text{not an outlier};\quad \text{Max } 21.8 > 21.6 \implies 21.8\text{ mm is an outlier.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate IQR:
$$20.7 - 20.1 = 0.6\text{ mm}$$

Calculate fences:
$$\text{Lower} = 19.2\text{ mm}, \quad \text{Upper} = 21.6\text{ mm}$$

Check endpoints:
$$19.4 \text{ is inside, } 21.8 \text{ is outside, so } 21.8\text{ mm is an outlier}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate IQR = 20.7 - 20.1 = 0.6 mm and range = 21.8 - 19.4 = 2.4 mm.
Calculate fences: 1.5 * IQR = 0.9 mm, lower fence = 20.1 - 0.9 = 19.2 mm, upper fence = 20.7 + 0.9 = 21.6 mm.
Conclude that minimum 19.4 >= 19.2 is not an outlier, but maximum 21.8 > 21.6 is an outlier.

hints: Recall that mean and standard deviation use all values and are sensitive to outliers.

Median and IQR depend on rank positions in the middle and are resistant.
Compare the consistency and reliability of the two production processes in context.

walkthrough.text:
Explain the sensitivity of mean and standard deviation:
$$\text{The competitor's outlier at } 21.8\text{ mm inflates both the sample mean and the standard deviation.}$$

Highlight the resistance of median and IQR:
$$\text{Median and IQR depend on the 50th and middle percentiles, providing an unaffected, resistant comparison.}$$

Evaluate relative consistency in context:
$$\text{The plant demonstrates superior manufacturing stability by avoiding rogue outliers beyond the tolerance fences.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Explain outlier effect:
$$\text{Outliers distort mean and standard deviation}$$

State resistant property:
$$\text{Median and IQR resist extreme values}$$

Evaluate process consistency:
$$\text{The plant avoids extreme outliers, showing greater stability}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that the competitor's data contains an outlier (21.8 mm), which distorts the mean and standard deviation.
Explain that the median and IQR are resistant measures that describe the true central location and middle 50% spread without being distorted by extreme values.

Compare consistency: the plant has standard deviation approximately 0.44 mm (equivalent to an estimated IQR of roughly 0.6 mm in symmetric normal data) whereas the competitor has an IQR of 0.6 mm, but the plant produces no extreme outliers, making the plant's production more reliably consistent.
